extracted.intended_audience: researchers, university administrators, diversity advocates, and policymakers interested in NIH grant review and racial disparities
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes how NIH R01 applications are evaluated (five criterion scores combined into a preliminary overall impact score) and reports a study analyzing racial disparities in those scores. Useful for understanding evaluation mechanics and evidence of bias in R01 peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five criteria on which assigned peer reviewers read applications and score them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assign a score for how important the research problem is; this score contributes to the overall preliminary impact score that predicts likelihood of advancing and receiving funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five criteria on which assigned peer reviewers read applications and score them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers judge novelty and creativity of concepts, approaches or technologies; the score is used (along with the other four criterion scores) to form the preliminary overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five criteria on which assigned peer reviewers read applications and score them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess the rigor, feasibility and quality of methods and study design; this criterion score factors into the preliminary overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five criteria on which assigned peer reviewers read applications and score them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate the qualifications, track record and suitability of the PI and team; this score contributes to the preliminary overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research environment
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five criteria on which assigned peer reviewers read applications and score them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess institutional and resource support for the project; the score is combined with the others to form the preliminary overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary overall impact score
rubrics_metrics.description: A composite score derived by reviewers who weigh the five criterion scores as they see fit; reflects the project's potential for major scientific impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The better the overall impact score, the more likely the application is to advance to discussion at the next round and ultimately receive funding. Assigned reviewers produce this preliminary score prior to panel discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer weighting of criterion scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers weigh the five individual criterion scores 'as they see fit' to derive the preliminary overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although weighting is part of the process, the UW study found that differences in how reviewers weigh the criterion scores do not explain black-white disparities in preliminary overall impact scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH 2009 five-criteria transparency framework
rubrics_metrics.description: The five evaluation criteria were introduced by the NIH in 2009 to add transparency to the R01 review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The framework was intended to make evaluation more explicit; however, the study notes that use of these five criteria did not reduce observed racial disparities in reviewer scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award rate (funding outcome) by applicant group
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric of the proportion of applications that receive funding, reported by applicant race in the study (example: 2014–2016 rates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study reports the overall award rate for Black researchers was 55% of that for white researchers (10.2% vs. 18.5% for 2014–2016), illustrating how score differences translate into differential funding outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for application and applicant characteristics in disparity analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytic standard to account for confounding variables (e.g., career stage, area of science) when evaluating whether score differences reflect bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The UW study controlled for key characteristics and still found Black researchers received worse scores on all five criteria, implying that observed disparities were not explained by those controlled factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential explanatory factors to investigate for score disparities
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate factors that may underlie observed racial disparities in criterion and overall scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors suggest investigating implicit racial preferences, choice of research topic, differences in mentorship and coauthor networks, emphasis on bibliometrics (such as citation counts), and the cumulative effect of disparities over a researcher’s career as possible contributors to why Black PIs are perceived as not excelling along specific evaluation dimensions.
